original_question: How do the ramification filtrations of Gal(L/K) and Aut_k(X_k) compare under the faithful injection of the finite monodromy group into the automorphism group of the special fiber of the stable model?
target_in_paper: The closest paper-faithful target is the introductory wild-monodromy problem in the contribution "Automorphisms of curves and stable reduction": after introducing the minimal finite monodromy extension L/K and the faithful action of Gal(L/K) on the special fiber of the stable model, the note asks how the wild monodromy is reflected in its action on that special fiber. The paper does not appear to state a separate formal general conjecture about equality of filtrations; the nearest explicit formulation is the setup preceding Definition 6.14 and the ensuing wild-monodromy questions.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the main objects that the paper relates: the minimal finite monodromy group Gal(L/K), its faithful injection into the automorphism group of the special fiber of the stable model, and the desire to compare arithmetic ramification data with geometric automorphism data on the special fiber.
missing_details: The ambient base must be specified: R should be a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0,p), with fraction field K and residue field k (algebraically closed in the standard setup used around the monodromy discussion).
One must specify that L/K is the minimal finite Galois extension over which the curve acquires semistable/stable reduction; this is the finite monodromy extension, not an arbitrary extension.

The curve must be identified: X_K should be a proper smooth projective geometrically connected curve over K; for the stable-model statement one needs g(X_K) >= 2 (the paper also mentions the semistable-reduction setup when g(X_K) >= 1 or X_K(K) is nonempty).
The model must be named: if 𝓧/R_L is the stable model of X_L := X_K ×_K L, then X_k denotes its special fiber.
The faithful map Gal(L/K) -> Aut_k(X_k) should be stated as coming from the extension of the Galois action on X_L to the stable model 𝓧.

It should be clear whether the question concerns the whole finite monodromy group Gal(L/K) or only its p-Sylow subgroup Gal(L/K)_w, the wild monodromy group. The nearby discussion in the paper focuses on wild monodromy.
The draft does not specify which ramification filtration is meant on Gal(L/K): lower numbering, upper numbering, or both. A stand-alone question must fix this.

The draft also does not specify what the comparison filtration on Aut_k(X_k) is supposed to be. One must say whether this is the filtration induced via the action at a chosen point/component/node of X_k, or the transported filtration on the image of Gal(L/K) inside Aut_k(X_k).

The mathematical force of 'compare' is not fixed: does one ask for equality after transport through the injection, for compatibility, for bounds, or merely for a geometric interpretation of successive ramification groups?

If the intent is filtration equality, the quantifier should be explicit: is this expected for every smooth projective X_K/K with stable reduction data as above, or only in the special p-cyclic / potentially good reduction situations emphasized by Lehr–Matignon?

The paper's explicit open questions are phrased in terms of determining the wild monodromy and its action on the special fiber in concrete examples, so a stand-alone reformulation should avoid overstating the existence of a formal universal conjecture unless one makes clear that this is an extraction from the setup rather than a verbatim statement.
refined_question: Let R be a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0,p), with fraction field K and residue field k, let X_K/K be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g(X_K) >= 2, let L/K be the minimal finite Galois extension over which X_K acquires a stable model 𝓧/R_L, and let X_k be the special fiber of 𝓧. Via the Deligne–Mumford faithful action, view Gal(L/K) as a subgroup of Aut_k(X_k). In what precise sense is the higher ramification filtration on the wild monodromy subgroup Gal(L/K)_w reflected by, or recoverable from, the action of its image on X_k; equivalently, can one read the wild monodromy filtration directly from the corresponding automorphism data on the stable special fiber?
justification: Your draft has the right core ingredients, but it is sharper than anything stated verbatim in the note: the note sets up the faithful action of the finite monodromy group on the special fiber and then focuses on understanding the wild monodromy and its action, especially in explicit examples. So the closest faithful stand-alone question is not a blanket equality claim between two unnamed filtrations, but a precise ask about whether the higher ramification filtration on the wild monodromy subgroup can be recovered from the induced automorphism action on the special fiber. That keeps the draft's intent while restoring the paper's hidden hypotheses and its actual focus on wild monodromy rather than arbitrary filtration language.
